clinician.trajectory_summary: A 7-year-old male with known proximal tubular dysfunction (SLC4A4 mutation) was admitted with acute right-sided weakness, left-sided headache, photophobia, phonophobia, fever, irritability, and altered cognition following superficial keratectomy. On admission, neurological examination showed mild distress, irritability, slight disorientation, and normal pupils with unremarkable systemic exam. Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging and MR angiography was unremarkable, excluding ischemic stroke or structural brain lesions. Lumbar puncture cerebrospinal fluid examination was unremarkable, excluding CNS infection. No prior or family history of migraine was documented. The clinical impression was hemiplegic migraine potentially triggered by emotional stress from anesthesia or use of vasoconstrictive drugs.
